chapter: Chicago and the wider jazz world
title: Ragtime tunes and Jelly Roll Morton lyrics
summary: Interviewers ask about Erskine Tate, Maple Leaf Rag and Jelly Roll; he vaguely recalls hearing the words.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: No, sir. No, sir. No, sir. No, sir.
I don't know about the Maple Leaf, yes. I don't know about the Frog Lake, I can't remember. It might have been that, but it wasn't that Frog Lake here.
I think that's James Scott or Scott Joplin. I can't remember which one. I think it's James Scott wrote that, you know. Scott Joplin wrote Maple Leaf and so many other
good ones. Easy one is one of my favorites. That's a pretty hot number.
Did you ever hear anyone sing a song about Jelly Roll, Jelly Roll, Forever On My Mind?
Jelly Roll. If I didn't, I can't record.
You made my poor mother crazy, you drove my poor daddy blind. Is that what the words I think? Mm-hmm. Original Jelly Roll Blues and the Jelly Roll Morton up in Chicago.
Just a set of words to that...

And it seems like that... It seems like that I wouldn't say now, you know, to be pretty going on it, but it seems like to me that I heard someone saying something about that. I heard parts of it somewhere. Oh, you did, huh? It seems like I did. Remember about when? It must have been a long time ago. Oh, yes, it was quite a bit ago. I can't recall now, but it seems like to me that, as you said, I got a mother on my mind. Well, they got two, three of those kind of good...
